methodology: Screened Arabic Quran 11:61–65 against published translations and examined candidate historical context. Search surfaced secondary claims about Thamūd and ancient Arabian inscriptions, but no inscription transcription, edition, date and provenance independently verified. Thus no earlier source relationship is public; absence of a specific parallel is preliminary, not a universal negative.

reviewed.topic: Ṣāliḥ addresses Thamūd, creation from earth and repentance
reviewed.notes: A named ancient Thamūd may be investigated through datable inscriptions; an ethnonym alone does not verify Ṣāliḥ or the narrated sermon.
A general ancestor-worship dispute does not establish a specific prior textual witness to this dialogue.

reviewed.topic: Ṣāliḥ invokes evidence, mercy and obedience
reviewed.notes: No specific earlier passage of this exchange has been checked; generic prophetic obedience parallels are inadequate.

reviewed.topic: She-camel as divine sign and prohibition of harm
reviewed.notes: No authenticated pre-Islamic textual account of Ṣāliḥ's she-camel established; do not conflate ancient camel iconography with this story.

reviewed.topic: Hamstringing the camel and three-day respite
reviewed.notes: Specific narrative and three-day period need traceable earlier witness; no pre-Islamic witness verified here.

research_dossier.title: Ṣāliḥ and Thamūd: call to repentance and she-camel (11:61–65)
research_dossier.chronology: Thamūd is a name discussed in ancient Arabian and external textual history. This batch does not authenticate any particular dated inscription or assert continuity of a single tribe over centuries.
research_dossier.comparative_discussion: Qur'an 11:61–63 narrates Ṣāliḥ's monotheistic appeal and opponents' objections; 11:64–65 narrates a protected she-camel and its hamstringing followed by three days' respite. No specific pre-Islamic narrative witness of these events has been established in this review.
research_dossier.variant_witnesses: Not yet collated. Later Muslim exegetical elaborations must be distinguished from earlier witnesses.
research_dossier.dating_caveat: Do not equate composition date, inscription carving date, first publication and surviving witness. The modern umbrella term 'Thamudic' for scripts does not by itself identify the historical Thamūd people or the Qur'anic narrative.
research_dossier.similarities_and_differences: No authenticated earlier passage available for direct textual comparison; neither borrowing nor independence can be inferred.
research_dossier.scholarly_interpretations: Any epigraphic or literary identification requires an attributed, source-specific scholarly argument, not name resemblance.
